summary.title: SQL editor still missing vim keybindings and real-time SQL linting
summary.text: Tabularis has Monaco autocomplete, but neither vim/emacs keybinding profiles nor inline SQL validation. Both are top pain points in DBeaver and TablePlus GitHub issues dating back to 2018-2019.

summary.title: Team collaboration is the #1 unmet complaint across both competitors
summary.text: Shared connections, query libraries, and role-aware workspaces appear across G2, Capterra, and TrustRadius for DBeaver. TablePlus has no team features at all. Tabularis has neither.

summary.title: Raw SQL transaction safety is a quick win with high user-safety impact
summary.text: TablePlus auto-commits raw SQL with no warning. A simple transaction mode toggle in the editor toolbar — small effort, high priority — would eliminate accidental data loss.

summary.title: Tabularis already leads on AI SQL, ER diagrams, and query history
summary.text: Both competitors have open unimplemented requests for AI SQL generation. Tabularis already ships multi-provider LLM support (including Ollama), interactive ER diagrams, persistent query history, and streaming CSV export — key differentiators where DBeaver and TablePlus fall short.

findings.title: Autocomplete is partial; vim keybindings and real-time linting are missing
findings.description: Tabularis has Monaco-based autocomplete with table/column/keyword suggestions. However, vim/emacs keybinding profiles are absent, and there is no real-time SQL linting — only syntax highlighting. Both gaps are top complaints in DBeaver (autocomplete freezes) and TablePlus (no vim, no bracket highlighting) GitHub issues.

quotes.text: Often, the processes freeze like this, and only a full program restart helps... if i click cancel request autocomplete not working till i restart program.
TablePlus is doing some internal queries and doesn't send the query in query editor to the database... with 100+ schemas it spends approximately 30 minutes downloading autocompletion information.

implementationSteps: Register Monaco vim mode extension in SqlEditorWrapper.tsx via a configurable keybinding profile setting.
Add a real-time SQL linting service using node-sql-parser or a WASM-based linter, wired into Monaco's setModelMarkers API.
Ensure the autocomplete provider in autocomplete.ts runs fully asynchronously — never block query execution while fetching schema metadata.
Add a keybinding profile selector (Default / Vim / Emacs) in Settings.

findings.title: Schema metadata loading and autocomplete can block on large databases
findings.description: Tabularis has pagination and streaming CSV export. However, the autocomplete provider and schema metadata fetcher may block query execution when databases have 100+ schemas — the exact issue that drove users away from TablePlus in 2025. DBeaver grows to 5 GB RAM and freezes with 5,000-line scripts.

quotes.text: DBeaver remained the one with most resident memory usage with a whopping 4.7GB RAM sitting at the htop while it was still struggling with simple scrolling.
With ~50,000 tables, loading the table list takes ~500 seconds due to SELECT * on information_schema.tables. The optimized query takes 0.4 seconds instead.

implementationSteps: Audit the schema metadata query in drivers/common/query.rs — ensure only table_name is fetched initially, not SELECT * on information_schema.
Move autocomplete schema loading to a background task that populates a cache lazily — never block the query pipeline.
Add a query cancellation signal from the UI through to the Tauri command layer.
Profile memory usage under a 50k-table schema and cap the metadata cache with an LRU eviction policy.

findings.title: No shared workspace, shared connections, or team query libraries
findings.description: DBeaver's team features are locked behind a paid self-hosted Team Edition. TablePlus has no team features whatsoever. Shared connections, query libraries, and role-aware workflows are the most-requested feature in DBeaver reviews across G2, Capterra, and TrustRadius. Tabularis has no implementation yet.

quotes.text: DBeaver does not have support for team collaboration I think, or if it is, it's not its strong point.

implementationSteps: Define a workspace data model with shared connections, saved queries, and member roles (owner / editor / viewer).
Implement cloud-sync for connection configs and query history via an optional backend service.
Add an invitation and member management UI.
Create a migration path from local-only saved assets to a shared workspace.

findings.title: Raw SQL queries execute with no transaction toggle or rollback warning
findings.description: TablePlus protects GUI edits with a review-and-commit step, but raw SQL auto-commits immediately. Tabularis has no transaction mode toggle in the SQL editor. A BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper with a visible rollback button would prevent accidental data loss — this is a small effort, high impact change.

quotes.text: Through the GUI all changes are temporarily made until they're committed. But no such safety for raw queries.
On the UI we can't find any button to execute a manual rollback command to revert the changes.

implementationSteps: Add a transaction mode toggle button to the SQL editor toolbar (auto-commit on / off).
When off, wrap DML execution in an explicit BEGIN on the Tauri commands layer.
Show the open transaction as a persistent status indicator with COMMIT and ROLLBACK buttons.
Persist the toggle preference per connection so power users don't reset it every session.

findings.title: Query history persistence across sessions
findings.description: Tabularis fully implements persistent query history per connection — stored in ~/.config/tabularis/query_history/{connectionId}.json with execution time, row count, deduplication, and configurable max entries. This is a paywalled feature in DBeaver Community and a persistent top-5 complaint.

quotes.text: Query Manager does not show history between sessions even when saving query logs to a file.

findings.title: Interactive ER/schema diagrams
findings.description: Tabularis fully implements interactive ER diagrams using ReactFlow + Dagre with pan, zoom, selective table display, and FK relationships as edges. Both DBeaver (read-only in Community) and TablePlus (plugin-only) leave this feature unfinished.

quotes.text: TablePlus lacks features such as creating entity relation diagrams and creating database schemas.

findings.title: No GUI for roles and permissions management
findings.description: TablePlus has shown a 'coming soon' placeholder for table privileges editing for years. DBeaver requires raw GRANT/REVOKE SQL. Tabularis has no visual roles or permissions matrix either — users who need to manage grants are forced to the command line.

quotes.text: Feature request to replace 'coming soon' message with a real table privileges editor for PostgreSQL — this feature has been 'coming soon' for years.

implementationSteps: Build a permissions matrix component: rows = tables/schemas, columns = roles.
Generate GRANT/REVOKE SQL statements from matrix edits and preview before applying.
Display current effective permissions per role/user.
Support PostgreSQL and MySQL permission models as a first pass.

findings.title: SSH tunneling works but ProxyJump and OPENSSH key format are unsupported
findings.description: Tabularis supports SSH tunneling with key authentication and keychain integration. However, ProxyJump directives in ~/.ssh/config are not honoured, and OPENSSH private key format (-----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----) may not be supported — the exact gaps that cause the most SSH frustration in TablePlus reviews.

quotes.text: The SSH support seems wonky... I can't get it to work with my ssh config which uses proxyjump.
Really challenging to use the SSH configuration, especially the jump server setup.

implementationSteps: Add ProxyJump/ProxyCommand parsing from ~/.ssh/config in the russh backend in ssh_tunnel.rs.
Verify OPENSSH key format (BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY) is handled by russh; add conversion fallback if not.
Expose a connection test in the SSH setup modal with actionable error messages.
Allow graceful fallback to system OpenSSH CLI for configs russh cannot handle.

findings.title: No in-place result set filtering without re-running the query
findings.description: Both DBeaver and TablePlus require re-running queries to narrow a result set. An inline filter bar — as in MySQL Workbench — would let users search and slice an already-fetched result client-side. Tabularis's DataGrid supports sorting but not dynamic in-place filtering.

quotes.text: Add a filter tab or inline filter bar on top of the query result set — similar to what MySQL Workbench offers. This allows quickly filtering existing results without rerunning the query.

implementationSteps: Add a collapsible filter bar above the DataGrid with a global text search input and per-column filter controls.
Implement client-side filtering on the fetched rows array — no re-query to the database.
Support filter operators: equals, contains, starts with, greater than, is null / is not null.
Preserve filter state across result refreshes so users don't lose their view.

findings.title: Streaming CSV export and import
findings.description: Tabularis implements streaming CSV export using futures::StreamExt with progress events every 100 rows and cancellation support. Both DBeaver and TablePlus fail on large files — TablePlus takes ~2 hours for 2.2M rows, DBeaver hangs on multi-million row imports. This is a clear competitive advantage.

quotes.text: Postgresql Import / Export is extremely slow and flawed — 2.2M rows CSV export took ~2 hours.

findings.title: AI-powered SQL generation and query explanation
findings.description: Tabularis already ships multi-provider AI SQL support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, OpenRouter, MiniMax) with text-to-SQL generation and query explanation. Both DBeaver and TablePlus have unimplemented GitHub feature requests for exactly this. This is a strong competitive differentiator.

quotes.text: The problem with TablePlus, DataGrip and most other GUIs for databases... they lack the 3 core features I want... AI-generated queries and reports.
